description: US-29 The customer balance. A hand-out today is PAID OR NOT PAID — DistributionRecord.paid is a boolean and the counter offers a checkbox. Reality has a third case DF have been writing in the Excel list by hand: the household owes 5,00 € and hands over 2,00 €, and — rarely — hands over MORE so as not to have to remember it next week. A checkbox loses it either way. This batch replaces the flag with an AMOUNT and derives ONE BALANCE per customer from the hand-out history. THE ARITHMETIC, and the one thing an implementer will get wrong: balance = Σ(paidCents − priceCents) over all of that customer's hand-outs, and amountToPay = max(0, priceCents − balance). The sum is against the PRICE, not against the amount asked for. Two quantities are in play and the requirement measures a different thing against each — an early draft used one German phrase, „geforderter Betrag“, for both, and was corrected and CONFIRMED WITH DF ON 2026-08-28. THE BALANCE (rule 2) is measured against the PRICE: read against the amount to pay the definition never settles — a household paying the full 8,00 € they were asked for gives 8,00 − 8,00 = 0 and their 3,00 € debt is still there to be charged again next week, and symmetrically a 3,00 € credit never shrinks and the household eats free for ever. THE COLOUR MARK (rule 10) is measured against the AMOUNT TO PAY — what was actually asked for that day — or a household clearing an old debt would read blue instead of green. Worked: price 5,00 paid 2,00 → balance −3,00; next week price 5,00, ASKED 8,00, paid 8,00 → balance 0. Price 2,00 paid 5,00 → +3,00; next week ASKED 0,00, paid 0,00 → balance +1,00 (the credit shrank by the week's price); next week ASKED 1,00. The amount ASKED FOR is still needed, for ONE purpose only: the colour mark on the record's history compares the payment against what was ASKED that day, so a household deliberately clearing an old debt reads GREEN (exact), not BLUE (over). askedCents is derived by replaying the history in order; NOTHING is stored to support it. THE CAP (US-26) caps the PRICE, never the amount to pay: an old debt is added on top of a capped price and is not itself capped. That falls out of the formula for free and must not later be 'fixed'. THE BALANCE IS NEVER STORED (ADR-015 in the last story) — a stored balance plus a hand-out history is two answers to one question, which is the Excel failure this project replaces; removing a hand-out then returns the balance for free. ON SCREEN: the counter gains its OWN PAYMENT ROW directly above the serve form — a large 'Zu zahlen' tile and a 'Saldo' tile — while the four derived tiles (Erwachsene | Kinder | Eier | Preis) are UNTOUCHED and the price stays in the fourth slot. NOBODY DOES SIGN ARITHMETIC: the balance is worded, never signed — „Guthaben 2,00 €“, „Offen 2,00 €“, „ausgeglichen“ — chosen on balanceKind and never on a comparison written in a component. The paid checkbox becomes a TEXT FIELD PRE-FILLED with the amount to pay; the normal case is confirming it, and it may be overwritten DOWN to 0,00 € without a question or UP with a CONFIRMATION — a mistyped credit is the one error the design cannot undo, and the confirmation is enforced by the USE CASE and not only by the screen. A payment is correctable only on the Berlin day it was recorded, unchanged from today. The record's history gains Gefordert and Gezahlt columns with a mark: paid short (red), paid exactly (green), paid over (blue), each carrying its meaning IN WORDS so colour only reinforces. A DEBT HAS NO AUTOMATIC CONSEQUENCE: the household is served normally and the staff member is informed, nothing more. NO note field on a payment, NO extra audit entry for a differing amount (the entries a hand-out, a correction and a removal already write are unchanged), NO debtors' overview, NO „Zahlung erfassen“ (settling a debt without a hand-out) — those two are deliberately deferred and DF's printed handout carries the human procedure that stands in for them: a mistake found after the day is put right by a compensating amount at the NEXT hand-out. SCHEMA CHANGE: paid Boolean becomes paidCents Int. Migration history is REGENERATED, not stacked on — confirmed with DF on 2026-08-28 that no real customer data exists (ADR-009) — and the hand-written partial unique index on Customer.customerNumber must be RE-ADDED. Fifth batch to do so. NO NEW PORT METHOD, but setPaid is RENAMED to setPayment, so every hand-written fake DistributionRecordRepository gains it in the same commit — including the one in read-group-roster.test.ts, which implements the port in full and has nothing to do with payments. Source: tasks/prd-us-29-customer-balance.md, written from local_only/new_requirement_balance_refined.md.

userStories.title: The balance arithmetic (domain)
userStories.description: As a developer, I need one pure module that turns a household's hand-outs into a balance and an amount to pay, so no screen and no use case does the sum of its own. Source: tasks/prd-us-29-customer-balance.md §US-29.1
acceptanceCriteria: New PURE module src/domain/distribution/balance.ts. No I/O, no clock, no import from Next.js, React or Prisma

PaidRecord = { readonly priceCents: Cents; readonly paidCents: Cents } — the two fields the arithmetic reads, and DELIBERATELY NOT DistributionRecord: the module is about money, and taking the whole record would let a later change drag a date or a customer id into a sum
balanceOf(records: ReadonlyArray<PaidRecord>): Cents returns Σ (paidCents − priceCents). It does NOT sort — a sum has no order — and returns 0 for an empty history

The doc comment carries the worked table from the PRD's Introduction and states in one sentence WHY THE SUM IS AGAINST THE PRICE AND NOT AGAINST THE AMOUNT ASKED FOR: read the other way the balance never settles — a household paying off its debt in full has the debt charged again next week, and a credit is never consumed by the week it pays for. This is the single most likely thing for a later reader to 'correct', so the comment must be explicit

amountToPay(priceCents: Cents, balanceCents: Cents): Cents returns Math.max(0, priceCents - balanceCents) — a debt raises it, a credit lowers it, and it NEVER goes below zero because credit is never paid out in cash

balanceKind(balanceCents: Cents): 'CREDIT' | 'DEBT' | 'SETTLED' — the ONE place the sign is read. Every screen asks this rather than comparing to zero itself, which is what keeps 'staff never do sign arithmetic' from being re-decided per screen
The module holds NO LIMIT OF ANY KIND: no floor, no ceiling, no warning threshold. DF's balances stay within ±20 € in practice and the software says nothing about it

STRICT TDD, invariant-breaking test first, one named test per rule: 'a household with no hand-outs is settled', 'a full payment leaves the balance where it was', 'a part payment leaves the shortfall open', 'paying more than the price leaves a credit', 'two shortfalls add up', 'a later payment settles an earlier shortfall', 'a debt raises the amount to pay', 'a credit lowers the amount to pay', 'a credit larger than the price leaves nothing to pay', 'a credit larger than the price is consumed by the week it pays for' (the week-4 row of the PRD table — THE NAMED TEST THAT PINS THE FORMULA), 'the amount to pay is never negative', 'a capped price plus an old debt exceeds the cap', 'names a positive balance a credit', 'names a negative balance a debt', 'names a zero balance settled'
domain/ stays at 100% coverage
Typecheck passes
Lint passes
Full unit suite passes: npm run test:coverage

userStories.title: The payment replay and the overpayment guard (domain)
userStories.description: As a staff member, I want each past hand-out to say what was asked and what was paid, so the record explains how the balance came about — and I want the one mistake that cannot be undone to be confirmed before it is written. acceptanceCriteria: PaymentStanding = 'SHORT' | 'EXACT' | 'OVER' and standingOf(paidCents, askedCents): PaymentStanding in balance.ts — the comparison is against the AMOUNT THAT WAS ASKED FOR, never against the price, so clearing an old debt is EXACT and not OVER

replayPayments<T extends PaidRecord & { date: Date }>(records: ReadonlyArray<T>) returns one Settlement<T> per record, OLDEST FIRST: { record: T; askedCents: Cents; standing: PaymentStanding; balanceAfter: Cents }

replayPayments SORTS ITS INPUT BY date ASCENDING ITSELF rather than trusting the caller. The order is the whole meaning of a running balance and the port that supplies the rows makes no promise about it — the same bargain createEggRule strikes by sorting inside the constructor. It sorts a COPY; the argument is not mutated

askedCents for each record is amountToPay(record.priceCents, balanceBefore), where balanceBefore is the running balance of every EARLIER record — so askedCents is exactly what the counter would have shown that day

A named test proves replayPayments(records).at(-1)?.balanceAfter === balanceOf(records) for a non-trivial history. Two functions that compute the same number from the same rows must never be able to disagree, and this is the test that says so
Do NOT add a settlementOf(settlements, recordId) helper. A caller wanting one record's asked amount finds it in the replay; a second lookup helper would be a second way to ask

New OverpaymentNotConfirmed in src/domain/errors.ts carrying paidCents and amountToPayCents, with its code added to DomainErrorCode and tiered 'refusal' in src/app/notice-tier.ts (the Record is exhaustive — the build fails until it is tiered, which is the mechanism working). The staff member is being asked a question, not shown a fault

The error's doc comment says what it is for: a mistyped credit is the one error this design cannot undo, because it silently pays for the household's next weeks. A SHORTFALL needs no confirmation — it shows up as an open amount at the very next hand-out

Tests written FIRST, named after the rule: 'marks a payment matching the amount asked as exact', 'marks a shortfall as short', 'marks a payment above the amount asked as over', 'marks clearing an old debt as exact, not over', 'marks paying nothing on a settled account as short', 'replays a history typed out of order', 'replays an empty history as nothing', 'states what was asked on the day, not what is asked today', 'agrees with the plain sum'

userStories.title: The documents describe the balance, and an ADR records the derivation
userStories.description: As the next developer — or DF themselves — I need the balance written down where the project already keeps its decisions and its instructions. Source: tasks/prd-us-29-customer-balance.md §US-29.10
acceptanceCriteria: ADR-015 'derive the customer balance from the hand-out history, never store it', recorded with the record-adr skill INCLUDING its row in the chapter 9 decision log. CONTEXT: CLAUDE.md grants exactly THREE exceptions to derive-don't-store, each with an argument of its own kind, and a running balance is the classic candidate for a fourth. DECISION: it is not one — a stored balance and a hand-out history are two answers to one question, and a removed or corrected record would leave them disagreeing silently, which is the Excel failure this project exists to replace. CONSEQUENCES, honestly: every read of a balance replays a customer's history (~50 rows a year, ~240 households, one distribution a week — irrelevant at this size, and the note SAYS SO), and a correction is automatically consistent for free
